title: Multi-Gateway Webhook Event Normalization & Exhaustive Narrowing
businessContext: A global subscription SaaS platform receives webhook events from Stripe, PayPal, and Adyen. Currently, developers use `any` casting, causing runtime crashes when payment gateway payload versions change or when unhandled event types slip through into billing ledger workers.
problemStatement: Build a strongly-typed webhook event dispatch system using discriminated unions and an exhaustive checking utility (`assertNever`). The compiler must enforce that every possible payment event type is handled at compile time, rejecting any PR that adds a new event without an exhaustive handler.
constraints: Zero usage of `any` or loose `unknown` casts.
Must enforce compile-time exhaustiveness: if a new event is added to the union, omission in the dispatcher must cause a TypeScript compilation error.
Must provide type narrowing on `event.payload` based on `event.provider` and `event.type`.
candidateTasks: Implement switch cases covering all union members with safe payload access.
Use `assertNever(event)` in the default branch to enforce compile-time verification.
Explain how discriminated unions differ from nominal typing or runtime schema validators like Zod.
hints: TypeScript can discriminate unions using literal string properties like `type` or combination of `provider` and `type`.
Passing `event` to `assertNever(event)` in `default` ensures that if any union case is omitted, TypeScript flags a type error because the variable has not been narrowed to `never`.
alternativeApproaches: Using a lookup object mapping event type to handler functions with Record<WebhookEvent["type"], (event: any) => string> constrained by generics.
Combining with Zod / Valibot for runtime validation at the HTTP edge before passing into typed domain logic.
commonMistakes: Using "as any" inside the cases instead of letting TypeScript naturally narrow the payload.
Forgetting the assertNever call, leaving unhandled cases silently ignored at compile time.
